title: Why Is Diesel Trading More Than $100 Above Crude?  | Presented by CME Group
description:
The diesel crack spread — the wholesale price of ultra-low sulfur diesel minus the cost of crude — reached a record $106 per barrel in early September, far above its typical $15–$40 range. With diesel powering the movement and production of goods, could this refined-product shortage feed into broader consumer inflation?  Presented by @cmegroup
